- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). **Diagnosis (done):**
- Root cause of slow load: `vite.config.ts` manualChunks catch-all `return "vendor"` merges ALL remaining node_modules into one 3.57 MB (1.09 MB gz) `vendor-*.js` that index.html loads eagerly. It contains @react-pdf + yoga (only used by dynamically-imported report generators — the careful code-splitting in [[report-gen-integration]] was defeated), recharts, stripe, capacitor.

- BottomNavigation already wraps setLocation in startTransition; PageTransition uses framer-motion AnimatePresence mode="wait" keyed on location.

1. ✅ Diagnose (above)
2. Fix manualChunks: drop the catch-all so dynamic-only deps stay in dynamic chunks

4. Skeleton loading states for retail/property/trades dashboards

The report generation feature (Task #59) is finished and verified. Here's where things landed:

**What I found:** far more was already built than the memory notes recorded — all 11 reports (4 property, 3 retail, 4 trades), the shared bottom-sheet modal, and the Export buttons were written and wired into all five dashboard/analytics pages. TypeScript, the 20 report-utils unit tests, and the production build all passed.

**What was actually broken — the lazy loading.** The whole design lazy-imports the ~1.4 MB @react-pdf engine so pages don't pay for it, but the vite `manualChunks` catch-all had swallowed it into the eagerly-loaded 3.5 MB vendor chunk, silently defeating that. Fixing it took two attempts:
- I first pinned @react-pdf's dependency tree to a manual `vendor-pdf` chunk. That backfired: a manual chunk reachable from the eager graph gets a side-effect import from the entry to preserve execution order, so the 1.4 MB still loaded on every page.
- The correct fix (converged with your parallel perf session, which removed the vendor catch-all in the same file while I worked) is **no manual chunk at all** — Rollup now colocates the PDF engine into a lazy `savePdf-*.js` chunk shared by the three report generators, fetched only when a merchant first hits Generate. I confirmed in the built output that nothing eager references it; index.html now preloads no PDF code.

**Visual verification (the piece that was still owed).** I built a headless harness (esbuild bundle with a Node `savePdf` stub) and rendered **all 11 PDFs plus the 3 CSVs** with realistic NZ fixture data, then inspected them page by page. The cover band, KPI cards, zebra tables, the landscape 12-month annual income matrix, the quote-conversion donut (correct at 40%), aged buckets, and the multi-client statement all render cleanly, and every total/GST figure cross-checks. CSV quoting is correct. Only nit: the "Balance outstanding" footer label wraps to two lines in the Client Statement — purely cosmetic.

I haven't committed — your other session is actively editing the same working tree (vite.config.ts changed three times while I worked), so a commit now would sweep up its in-flight changes. Everything is in the working tree ready to commit whenever you want; memory notes are updated to reflect the completed state.
